n: Philip Johnson (1906-2005), working with John Burgee, designed the AT&T Headquarters (1978-1983) in New York, a pivotal early Post-Modern skyscraper.

q: The Paul Revere House (1680s), an example of American Colonial Architecture, is located in which city?
n: The Paul Revere House, built in the 1680s in Boston, Massachusetts, is one of the earliest surviving examples of American Colonial Architecture (1620-1820s).

q: I.M. Pei designed the National Center for Atmospheric Research (1961-1967) in which Colorado city?
n: Pei (1917- ) designed the National Center for Atmospheric Research in Boulder, Colorado, an American Brutalist landmark completed between 1961 and 1967.

q: The Turner-Ingersoll House, a Colonial-era structure from the 1700s, is located in which Massachusetts city famous for witch trials?
n: The Turner-Ingersoll House dates to the 1700s and stands in Salem, Massachusetts; it is also known as the 'House of the Seven Gables.'

q: Gordon Bunshaft designed the Hirshhorn Museum, completed in 1974, in which city?
n: Bunshaft (1909-1990) designed the Hirshhorn Museum in Washington, D.C., in 1974, a cylindrical Brutalist museum building.

q: Thomas Jefferson designed Monticello, his home begun in the 1770s, in which Virginia city?
n: Jefferson (1743-1826) designed Monticello near Charlottesville, Virginia, a personal architectural statement of Neo-Classical ideals begun in the 1770s.

q: Richard Meier designed the Barcelona Museum of Contemporary Art (1995) and the Getty Center (1997) in which American city?
n: Meier (1934- ) designed the Getty Center in Los Angeles, completed in 1997, alongside the Barcelona Museum of Contemporary Art in the same decade.

q: Charles Bulfinch designed the Old State House (1796) in Hartford, Connecticut, and also designed which Boston building, begun in 1798?
n: Bulfinch (1763-1844) designed both Hartford's Old State House (1796) and Boston's Massachusetts State House, begun in 1798, key Federal Style works.

q: Frank Gehry designed the Walt Disney Concert Hall (1991-2003) in Los Angeles and the Guggenheim Museum (1993-1997) in which Spanish city?
n: Gehry (1929- ) designed the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao, completed 1997, using the same sculptural, titanium-clad Deconstructivist language as his later Walt Disney Concert Hall.

q: Richard Upjohn designed Trinity Church in New York, completed in the 1840s, in which style?
n: Upjohn (1802-1878) designed New York's Trinity Church in the 1840s, a leading example of American Gothic Revival Architecture (1760s-1840s).

q: Which architectural movement, spanning roughly the 1980s to 2000s, includes Frank Gehry's Walt Disney Concert Hall and Peter Eisenman's Wexner Center?
n: Both buildings belong to Deconstructivism (1980s-2000s), a movement known for fragmented, non-orthogonal forms.

q: Which two American buildings, both called the 'Old State House,' were designed by Charles Bulfinch?
o: The Boston and New York buildings
The Hartford, Connecticut and Boston (Massachusetts State House) buildings
n: Bulfinch designed Hartford's Old State House (1796) and, under the Federal Style entry, Boston's State House project begun in 1798.

q: Which architect's Getty Center (1997) in Los Angeles is classified under Neo-Rationalism?
n: Richard Meier (1934- ) designed the Getty Center in Los Angeles, completed in 1997, part of the Neo-Rationalism period (1980s-1990s).

q: Henry Hobson Richardson designed the Stoughton House in the 1880s in which Massachusetts city?
n: Richardson (1838-1886) designed the Stoughton House in Cambridge, Massachusetts, in the 1880s, an example of Victorian-era shingle massing.

q: John Wood the Elder designed which curved terrace of townhouses in Bath, England, begun in the 1750s?
n: John Wood the Elder (1695-1753) laid out The Circus, a circular ring of townhouses in Bath, in the 1750s. His son, John Wood the Younger, later completed the Royal Crescent nearby.

q: Henry Hobson Richardson designed the Marshall Field Warehouse (1885-1887) in which city?
n: Richardson designed the Marshall Field Warehouse in Chicago between 1885 and 1887, a monumental commercial building in his Romanesque style.

q: Robert Adam was commissioned in 1759 to remodel which English country house in Derbyshire?
n: Robert Adam (1728-1792) took the Kedelston Hall commission in 1759, one of his earliest major works in the Neoclassical style he helped popularize in Britain.

q: Queen Anne Style (1870s-1910) and Mission Style (1890-1915) are cross-referenced to which two broader categories, respectively?
o: Victorian Architecture and Arts and Crafts
Gothic Revival Architecture and Prairie Style
n: Queen Anne Style falls under Victorian Architecture, while Mission Style is grouped with the Arts and Crafts movement.

q: Claude-Nicolas Ledoux is associated with a utopian city plan for which French town, drawn up in the 1770s?
n: Ledoux (1736-1806) designed an idealized industrial town plan for Chaux, France, in the 1770s, reflecting Enlightenment ideas about rational urban planning.

q: Richardsonian Romanesque architecture in America spans roughly which period?
n: Richardsonian Romanesque is dated roughly 1870s-1900, distinct from but overlapping the broader Victorian Architecture period of 1860-1900.

q: Karl Friedrich Schinkel designed the Altes Museum, completed in 1822, in which city?
n: Schinkel (1781-1841) completed the Altes Museum in Berlin in 1822, a landmark of German Neoclassicism with its long Ionic colonnade.

s: Beaux-Arts and Arts & Crafts Architecture in America
q: The 1893 World's Columbian Exposition, a major showcase of Beaux-Arts planning, was held in which city?
n: The World's Columbian Exposition of 1893 took place in Chicago, promoting the classical Beaux-Arts style across the country afterward.

q: Roughly when was Robert Adam commissioned for Kedelston Hall in Derbyshire, England?
n: The Kedelston Hall commission dates to 1759, early in Robert Adam's career developing his signature Neoclassical style.

s: Beaux-Arts and Arts & Crafts Architecture in America
q: Carrere and Hastings designed the Morgan Library (1906) and which major library building in New York, 1897-1911?
n: John Carrere (1858-1911) and Thomas Hastings (1860-1929) designed the New York Public Library (1897-1911) as well as the Morgan Library and Pennsylvania Station.

s: Gothic Revival, Romantic & Beaux-Arts Architecture in Europe
q: Charles Barry designed the Houses of Parliament in London between 1830 and the 1860s. Which co-designer handled the Gothic detailing?
n: Barry (1795-1860) was responsible for the overall plan, while Pugin (1812-1852) designed the Gothic Revival ornament and interiors of the Houses of Parliament.

s: Beaux-Arts and Arts & Crafts Architecture in America
q: Which New York museum, a Beaux-Arts landmark, opened in 1895?
n: The Metropolitan Museum of Art's Beaux-Arts building in New York dates to 1895, part of the wave of grand civic buildings following the 1893 Columbian Exposition.

s: Gothic Revival, Romantic & Beaux-Arts Architecture in Europe
q: John Nash designed the Royal Pavilion, built 1815-1832, in which English seaside town?
n: Nash (1752-1835) designed the Royal Pavilion in Brighton, notable for its exotic Indo-Saracenic domes, an example of Romantic architecture's taste for eclectic historical revivals.

s: Beaux-Arts and Arts & Crafts Architecture in America
q: Charles Sumner Greene and Henry Mather Greene designed the Gamble House (1908) in which California city?
n: The Greene brothers designed the Gamble House in Pasadena, California, in 1908, a celebrated Arts and Crafts (Craftsman) style bungalow.

s: Gothic Revival, Romantic & Beaux-Arts Architecture in Europe
q: The Cotswold Cottage style, popular from the 1890s to 1940s, is classified under which broader revival style?
n: Cotswold Cottage-type houses are grouped under the Tudor Revival Style, which drew on English vernacular half-timbered building traditions.

s: Beaux-Arts and Arts & Crafts Architecture in America
q: Which firm's work included the Boston Public Library, the Rhode Island State Capitol, and employed the partners McKim, Mead, and White?
n: The firm McKim, Mead & White — Charles McKim, William Mead, and Stanford White — designed both the Boston Public Library and the Rhode Island State Capitol.

q: Antoni Gaudí designed the Sagrada Familia and Palau Guell in which Spanish city, both begun in the 1880s?
n: Gaudí (1852-1926) built most of his major Art Nouveau (Catalan Modernisme) works in Barcelona, including Palau Guell, Sagrada Familia, and later Casa Mila (1905).

s: Prairie, Expressionist, and Art Deco Architecture in America
q: Frank Lloyd Wright and Marion Mahony Griffin designed the Frederick C. Robie House (1906-1909) in which city?
n: Wright (1867-1959), working with Marion Mahony Griffin (1871-1961), designed the Robie House in Chicago, a landmark of the Prairie Style (1900-1920s).

q: Victor Horta's 1892 Tassel House, an early Art Nouveau landmark, is located in which city?
n: Horta (1861-1947) built the Tassel House in Brussels in 1892; its exposed iron structure and curving lines are considered one of the first true Art Nouveau buildings.

s: Prairie, Expressionist, and Art Deco Architecture in America
q: Bruce Goff designed the Ledbetter House (1947) and the Bavinger House (1950s), both in which Oklahoma city?
n: Goff (1904-1982) designed both experimental houses in Norman, Oklahoma, known for unconventional, organic Expressionist forms.

q: Hector Guimard is best known for designing the entrances to which Art Nouveau transit system, 1899-1905?
n: Guimard (1867-1942) designed the distinctive cast-iron and glass entrance canopies for the Paris Metro between 1899 and 1905.

s: Prairie, Expressionist, and Art Deco Architecture in America
q: Eero Saarinen designed the Trans World Airport (TWA) Terminal in New York, completed in which range of years?
n: Saarinen (1910-1961) designed the TWA Terminal between 1956 and 1962, celebrated for its swooping, bird-like concrete shell.

q: Charles Rennie Mackintosh designed the Glasgow School of Art (1897-1909) and which Scottish house, 1902-1904?
n: Mackintosh (1868-1928) designed Hill House in Helensburgh, Scotland (1902-1904), alongside his Glasgow Herald Building (1893-1895) and Glasgow School of Art.

s: Prairie, Expressionist, and Art Deco Architecture in America
q: Raymond Hood also designed the New York Daily News Building, completed in which year?
n: Hood designed the New York Daily News Building in 1929, following his Chicago Tribune Tower success five years earlier.

q: Which architect designed both the Palau Guell and the Sagrada Familia, two Barcelona landmarks begun in the 1880s?
n: Antoni Gaudí (1852-1926) began both Palau Guell and the still-unfinished Sagrada Familia in the 1880s, defining Catalan Art Nouveau.
